steps.text: Wait, this is... Babel?!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: With the help of his friends, the puppet crossed the river of tears, and even the golden ocean behind them they didn't know about...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Finally, they set foot on land once again, and found that Plains of Hope.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa, do you like the ending I came up with?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Of course I do.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The puppet's friends—that's my favorite part of your story.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But... how did the story actually end, Theresa?
...Theresa?
I can't recall ever having this conversation with Theresa, but I've dreamed of it happening countless times.
It meant the story would finally get an ending it never had, and that the storyteller never left.
I want to tell her I already have the power to change how the story ends.
The question I wasn't able to answer back then, and the answer I've found—
I am willing and able to bear this crown.

options: Amiya!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'Metal matter, fall like feather.'

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: There's no way we can stabilize this huge-ass thing! We'll end up a smear on the ground at this rate!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Time to get to work, ancestor!

steps.name: Revenant's Voice
steps.text: I am trying! Regaining control of this ship is no easy feat!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Quit pretending! How were you so good at it when you were working for the Military Commission?

steps.name: Revenant's Voice
steps.text: Insolence! Treat your elders with more respect, young Sarkaz!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We have to brace ourselves for the impact from the airship's emergency landing. Mon3tr, protect the Doctor and Amiya.
Dr. Kal'tsit... they need me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, the puppet's friends never gave up on him. No matter how they suffered...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Whenever the puppet needs them, they'll show up, catch him, and walk him through his troubles together.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That's what I wish for too. I hope I'll always be there whenever you need me.
—She's looking at... me?
Theresa...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But what we go through... things don't always go our way.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Some of the little puppet's friends will get lost while on their journey.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But their collective memories will accompany their little puppet friend to the end.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya... I will always be with you all.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Regardless of what form I take.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are you... leaving?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What are you saying, Amiya? I left long ago.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You're... not Theresa.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, the memories in your dreams are warm. But you should wake up now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Return to your companions, Amiya. They need you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Your journeys have yet to end.
How did I end up here?
We just... left the Assimilated Universe—
I remember the airship returning to our familiar sky, Originium crystals covering the entire ship receding like the tide...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: This is the most I can do with my incantations. I'm afraid there's no way to absorb all the impact force.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I'm trying my best here! One more time, old coot!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr!
Everyone... needs me...
What can I even do now...?
Every inch of the gigantic ship vibrates in a metallic shudder.
The airship's speed of descent slows down once more.
She uses everything Theresa has taught her with all her strength to prop up the monstrously huge vessel.
A warm power like a murmur from her dreams encircles Amiya.
She feels as if that person who left has returned, hugging her.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa...
Amiya has never experienced a feeling like this.
The 'Civilight Eterna's power enveloping her, abundant and warm.
Is this an illusion? Or is she still dreaming?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa...? Is that really you?

steps.name: Theresa?
steps.text: Well done, Amiya.

steps.name: Theresa?
steps.text: You have to believe in your comrades, and your own strength too.

steps.name: Theresa?
steps.text: We'll descend slowly.
Every Sarkaz on the battlefield raises their head, as if sensing a familiar aura.
The silhouette of a supposedly-dead King of Sarkaz appears in the radiance.
With a sigh, they no longer see her, only a gentle Cautus with a similar form to the person they were expecting to see.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: We... landed safely, I guess? Was that old thing actually useful, or...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Bunny? Why do you look like...?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wiš'adel...? What about me...?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Forget it!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Did we end up in Londinium? The Shard doesn't seem so far away.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes... The airship is a huge target, so the Sarkaz stationed within the city will soon come looking for us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We'll have to evacuate as quickly as we can.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I have something better in mind.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa... no, you're not...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm the only one who can see you, right?

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: Yes. Others can see me as well, only if you wish it so.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Just who are you...?

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: A promise.

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: Theresa promised to stay by your side and watch you grow up.

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: Theresa is gone forever, but she left a program inside the crown—I manifested in this form because of your emotions.
A promise, an emotion entrusted into the crown, a will that relies on 'Civilight Eterna' to exist.

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: Do you have any doubts, Amiya? I can answer them.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If Theresa truly left you here as her will...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The story about the puppet, and its ending... What was it that Theresa wanted to tell me?

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: Theresa made up that story herself, and there are no records of it in any existing works.

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: So there is no way I can answer your question.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: But you have surpassed her, as she wished.

steps.name: Theresa's Phantom
steps.text: What she wanted to say has already been passed on to you. It's up to you to decide what will happen next in the story.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thank you... Theresa.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Did you guys see that? The Sarkaz airship fell from the sky!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: The clouds—they're scattering!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: The Sarkaz can't control the storm anymore!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Amiya and the Doctor did it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No matter how short or long this moment of safety lasts, we must seize the opportunity—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Capture Silverrock Bluffs, and advance toward the city walls.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: ...Rout the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: ...Today, the second time.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: We witnessed her departure.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: A great King of Sarkaz, a true hero.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: She initiated an unprecedented grand undertaking for the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: And we... are witnesses, and participants.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: From the Royal Court camps to the War Council, and to the Military Commission of today—

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: We will never fall as long as war still goes on. We have already wrested enough victories for the Sarkaz over the past millennia.
He looks up at the dreadful scene in the sky with only reverence.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The Victorians zealously chase after the phantom of victory while never understanding of why we crave war in the first place.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: ...'From death comes new life'.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Hah. This war has sated me.
'The 106th Assault Artillery Brigade has successfully regrouped with the 2nd and 8th Battalions of the Duke of Normandy's Grenadier Regiments!'
'9th Battalion Armored Corps and The Exemplars have seized control of Hill 92!'
'Anti-Witchcraft cannons back online!'

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Mid-range communication has been restored.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Your Grace, the battlefield is back under our control.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...What of him?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Gastrell is severely damaged, and should still be—

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Hold on, we just managed to locate it!

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: It's—right next to us!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Your Grace, an urgent telegram from the Duke of Gododdin.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...Have our forces dispatched to Duskglow River withdraw at once.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Yes, Your Grace.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Your Grace...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...Were we late?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: All frequencies... went down simultaneously. He blinded every single eye of ours.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: That Duke of Wellington...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Many years ago, by the Duskglow River... he told me a day would come when nothing would be able to stop the advance of high-speed battleships.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: He's done it.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Your Grace, the Gastrell has paused its advance!

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Iron Duke's warships are forming up again!

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Three light battleships have turned their guns toward—

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Isn't that the Duke of Wellington's ship?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: ––What the bloody hell are they doing?!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: The Sarkaz have only just retreated, but he wants to start another war with the dukes right away?! Has he truly gone mad?!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The dead... that fire in their eyes...
The nearby 'Adjutant Hill' stops in his tracks.
The purple fire leaves from his eyes, floating to someplace higher, further away.
To shadows and smoke enshrouding an entire fleet of steel.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Your Royal Highness Eblana, are you ready?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Anytime.
Flame falls from the sky, rolling across the flagship's bow, burning the original flag instantly.
Similar fires blossom in purple one after the other on every ship in Wellington's fleet.

steps.name: Taran Citizen
steps.text: Huh? What day is it today? What's with the fireworks?

steps.name: Taran Citizen
steps.text: Heck, not just that—Isn't that the municipal building? What was that they just rolled down from up there—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: It's a new flag.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: We worked so hard just for today, you know.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: So? Looks nice, doesn't it?

steps.name: Taran Child
steps.text: Thank you for the flower, Miss Reed! It's so pretty!

steps.name: Taran Child
steps.text: What are you looking at, Miss?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Um... we are quite a distance from Londinium, yes?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Could the ashes from the battlefield float this far?
A spark falls on the Draco's fingertip.
The fleeting purple fades, leaving only a speck of dull grey ash.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...It's hot.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: ...Tara.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: After a century, we finally raise our flag once more on this land.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: We have proved our strength to the Sarkaz and the Victorians.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Here and now, no one will be able to stop us, to scorn us.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Tarans—my people, they shall become a force that can control the war, and shape the land.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: We shall let everyone see the coming of a new age.
The Draco raises her hand, smiling at the land.
Every Taran flag flutters in unison.
A rich purple coalesces under the clouds—
Finally, it stands against the crimson storm and the still flickering golden light.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: He really has no intention of letting us breathe.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Wellington...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Do you truly hate Victoria, or...?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Your Grace, an urgent telegram from the Duke of Gododdin.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And the Duke of Normandy, as well as the Duke of Fife...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Let them sit in their anxiety for a while.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Back then, we joined hands to confine this warmonger into a duke's attire. Now we have no choice but to suffer the consequences of our actions.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Go, fetch the proposal locked away in the first drawer on the right side of my desk.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I wrote it myself... before I came to Londinium.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Will the Iron Duke... be willing to restart negotiations?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: No, that's not it.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Victoria will no longer have an Iron Duke in future.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But Caster may perhaps find a new powerful ally.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: By reforging an alliance with Wellington at this time?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: This is in our best interests.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: He knows I will make this choice. He and King Gaeil's descendant... treat war and death like their bargaining chips.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: We must recognize Tara's independence if we don't wish to go to war on two fronts at this critical juncture.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Our soldiers and people will be furious once they find out about Wellington's betrayal. They won't accept our choice so easily either.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...Indeed.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But what of it?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: The people have always longed for a 'hero' that descends from the heavens to guide them.
The Duke casts her gaze toward the battlefield below.
The soldiers are excitedly chanting a name in the wake of their fresh decisive victory—
'Exemplars'.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: She certainly doesn't resemble her father.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Other than her golden hair... speaking of which, it's amusing how legitimate heirs to the Aslan royal line always sport such dazzling hair that you can see it shine from afar.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You mean...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Heh. Ah, Alexandrina. That girl might just be Victoria's chosen one.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The ducal fleets are restructuring their formation...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They're...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Slowing their pursuit?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: So that's why the cannons go all quiet?! What are they thinking? The Sarkaz only just retreated, so now's the best time to give them a thrashing!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: That's Gododdin's frigate.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: They're approaching... the wreck of Caster's flagship. Seems like he's taking the opportunity for a breather.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Just that?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: It's probably because he's scared the ship's going to take so long to repair that the Nachzehrers will rush onto the deck and devour them all.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: When's the last time we saw Londinium's walls?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Are they cracked wide open? Covered with Originium crystals? Or soaked in fresh blood, all covered with dead branches, or even inlaid with the bones of our people?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: When we got out of Norport, many of us might have thought that was the worst we'd experience.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But afterwards we saw a deck flooded with blood, and went through a perilous time all thanks to the Originium.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We watched as the war turned our city into an unrecognizable ruin.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is there anyone willing to puff out their chest and say they can imagine how the city looks like inside?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The dukes' spies should have more information than we do.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: From their conduct, Caster and the others are probably preparing to abandon Londinium.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: A nomadic city wrecked by Sarkaz may be worth less than a fleet formed at a high price.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Also... the Shard has truly yet to fall. No one knows if the Sarkaz have any remaining tricks to try, or if another city will turn into a battlefield.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: More nobles might decide to move their troops back home.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Blast it! I knew they'd pull something like that!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Win a tough fight, and then not give a crap about what's gonna happen to Londinium!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Yes. As you say, that's what they'd definitely do. So it's just another ordinary day for Victoria.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: As for us—we've decided long ago what we should do, haven't we?
Siege walks into the crowd.
For a moment, she cannot discern if someone belongs to the Exemplars or was saved by them.
Everyone is exhausted, but they still hold their heads up high.
Siege knows she doesn't have to say much.
Because opened eyes will not close so easily anymore.
Everyone watches Siege.
Siege looks toward Londinium, their city, their people.
She lifts the hammer in her hand.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Exemplars—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Advance!

steps.name: Scared Sarkaz Soldier
steps.text: Enough... enough! Please, just withdraw the order!

steps.name: Scared Sarkaz Soldier
steps.text: The Shard has already stopped, so how can we go on fighting?

steps.name: Scared Sarkaz Soldier
steps.text: What else can we do now but to be smashed into paste by a high-speed battleship?

steps.name: Low-Ranking Sarkaz Officer
steps.text: Shut up! Shut that *Sarkaz expletive* mouth of yours!

steps.name: Low-Ranking Sarkaz Officer
steps.text: We are at war, and this is the battlefield! Hide in here all you want, and some Feline will eventually lop your head off anyway!

steps.name: Low-Ranking Sarkaz Officer
steps.text: Pick up your blade! If we must die, we die with dignity!

steps.name: Low-Ranking Sarkaz Officer
steps.text: There's no other way we can go!

steps.name: Low-Ranking Sarkaz Officer
steps.text: What's going on...? Who else could use the Royal Court's frequency? Whose signal is this?
Hello? Hello? Can anyone hear me?
Wiš'adel's the name—the one and only name granted by Her Highness The King of Sarkaz Theresa herself.
Every Sarkaz still under the Military Commission's command, listen up.
I don't care if you came here after hearing whatever nonsense from Theresis or some Royal Court geezer.
I'm delighted to announce: the war has ended, and you guys lost.
But Her Highness says she wants to have every Sarkaz return home.
So, if you want to live, it's time to ignore orders from the Military Commission and do as this transmission says.
Oh, I should've mentioned it earlier.
This is Babel.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Quick, follow me!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: This path is safe, we haven't spotted any Sarkaz for the time being!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: A transmission?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Our own Exemplar frequency... Miss Closure!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm listening! Turn the volume up... some more...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Everyone should be able to hear it now.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Wow... did I hear that right?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: That Siege lady did it! She brought back our people with her, and together pave a way...

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: ...A way home.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: We've sent a squad closest to their location over. Fang's squad is also on their way. She's the fastest out of them and can help us ensure the road stays clear.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Next, I just have to find a relatively safe spot for the rendezvous...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: No need for that.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Miss Closure, we're quite close to the city walls.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Every maintenance access point... is inside my head.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Every member of the Self-Salvation Corps who pulled out from Londinium won't forget them.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: There are some very old passages the Sarkaz definitely have no clue about.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: We can go home.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: That frequency you care about is active.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: Judging from their speed, they're practically rushing toward the city.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: The passages the Sarkaz don't know about only number a few.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: They'll definitely pick the path closest to Highbury.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Something happened in there before. Feist won't risk that with his party.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: It's probably K15. If they go through somewhere else, spread some news about Munitions Factory No. 11 and figure a way to lure them there.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: Same rules as usual?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Yes. Clean that path up as much as you can.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: And don't get spotted when we make a kill, yeah?

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: You're more wary with these regular workers and 'The Exemplars' than you are with the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: In case something does go awry, could you just let me know if you see them as friend or foe?

spans.text: go awry, could you just let me know if you see them as friend or foe?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: That doesn't matter. The person they knew is no longer here.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: That disgraceful traitor died in the Mausoleum of Kings, and... is no longer worthy of retrieving the glory they threw away themselves.
She hears a faint familiar sound once more.
Again and again, agitating her eardrums and heart.
But there is no white steam in the sky at all.
Perhaps, it is merely the sound of Active Originium rapidly evaporating into the air.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: That armor... did it fly away?

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: We haven't gotten any news.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: The Sarkaz might have taken it apart, or maybe Originium buried it on the battlefield.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: You achieved your goal for now by leading it to the Sighs of Kings to help the Exemplars out. But it's really difficult to control. Do we have to figure out a way to retrieve it?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Let's not risk ourselves with that yet.

steps.name: Victorian Mercenary
steps.text: Sure, I mean, it might just pop out on its own accord whenever. Who knows what a mad ghost would want to do next?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Perhaps...

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Or maybe, when next we meet, he can find a bit of... something that belongs to him.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: *cough* *cough* No, absolutely NOT! You know just how rare it is to find protective gear able to cope with high levels of Originium in Londinium nowadays!

steps.name: Nervous Citizen
steps.text: But, your price is just too—

steps.name: Nervous Citizen
steps.text: We have a lot of people in our community who needs these, so can't you just cut it down...?

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: You just told me your wife and child have stones growing on them, and they can't bear with the pain—

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: I'll be frank. Me too! Every night it gets so bloody painful I can't catch a wink!

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: I suspect the same goes for everyone in this city. These wretched crystals are growing wantonly on everybody!

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Not to mention those devils anxiously running amok now.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: So, listen well. My price is fairer than fair. You're worried for your health, but I have to plan for my future.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Columbia's private sanatoriums don't come cheap. I know a director there who's a cunning scoundrel, and I only hope he doesn't con me out of my coin.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: I also have to pay my servants, my chef...

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: What's going on?!

steps.name: Security Detail
steps.text: Mr. Hall, they're currently—

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Have the Sarkaz found us? Hurry, get moving! And push out those paupers still clinging around our doorway to buy some time! Those devils can't tell whose lives are more valuable!

steps.name: Security Detail
steps.text: No, that's not it! They're not Sarkaz!

steps.name: Security Detail
steps.text: Blast it, they've smashed in our warehouse wall! Now everyone's rushing in to grab the goods inside and we can't stop them!

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: What do I pay you for?! Where are your electrical nets and heavy crossbows? I don't care if you attract some Sarkaz as long as you keep the goods safe!

steps.name: Security Detail
steps.text: B-But they have fire on their side—

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Fire?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Good day, Mr. Hall.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: ...I know you people—

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: 'Reunion', right? The city has been all abuzz about your group these past few days.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Listen to me, Reunion. I don't know why there's a misunderstanding between us—I'm Infected too!

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: We're basically family, right? We can work together!

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Just name a price—how much for you to be my bodyguards?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Reunion does not accept employment offers.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Then—ngh, what about a share of my sales? Or a donation?

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: I can make a donation as an Infected! The city's Infected need all of these urgently, aren't we the people you fight for?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Heh. 'Donation'? That's not the tune you were whistling earlier.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: I see, I get it now. I should have thought of it earlier.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: Ha! Of course, of course... everyone would want all of this for themselves—you're just capitalizing on another crime!

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: You want to set the score? Sure, I'll begin.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Stewart Hall. You applied for a huge subsidy every year for protective equipment because your factory processes Originium.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: But your workers have never seen a single garb of protective gear you've accumulated. The Infected living in the outskirts of town—just how many of them were your workers who were kicked out from your factory?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Meanwhile, you stuffed yourself with Columbian pioneer company meetings. Failing to send all these gear out before war broke out in Londinium must have cost you a pretty penny.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: But you still thought yourself lucky. Londinium's done for, and the protective suits you almost deemed a loss came in handy once again.

steps.name: Fretful Merchant
steps.text: You... just what do you people want?! Are you not a group that liberates the Infected? Look, just look at the stones all over my body—

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Physical illness is not the source of the Infected's suffering—it is injustice.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Your luck has run out, Mr. Hall.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Because Reunion is here.

steps.name: Nervous Citizen
steps.text: You're Talulah, right? I've heard of you, it's all thanks to you—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Just doing what I should do.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: This is a lot of protective suits we have here. We'll have to distribute them...

spans.text: of protective suits we have here. We'll have to distribute them...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Even if infection is inevitable for some, this equipment can slow the disease's progression for those already sick. At the very least, they won't suddenly explode into bits from continuous exposure in a high level Originium zone.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: But most Infected choose to hide in their homes, so they wouldn't know who to ask for help even if their condition gets terribly dire, right?

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: So let us go look for them.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Tommy, you know how dangerous that is.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Of course. That odd thing hanging above the Shard seems to be gone, and the sky seems to have lightened up a little.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Guess the Sarkaz are having some trouble. Our blokes are saying a huge amount of Sarkaz are retreating into the city.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: They're also swarming the spot where that flying fortress fell. According to the current alert level, going out is practically suicide.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Then you still—

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: We were doomed long ago, right?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: ...I understand.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: My brother lives in County Castshire, you've met him. If I don't make it back, just give my wrench to him. If... if possible, tell him I was a...

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Nah, forget it. Tell him nothing.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Also, Catherine. My stance towards you, Feist, the Self-Salvation Corps and Rhodes Islanders has never changed.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: There's no meaning in saying that. What's happened won't change.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: But you can influence and change whatever's yet to happen, kid.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Hah!

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Then... we're all good to go.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: That's quite brave of them.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You've spent quite some time staring at some of those punks.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: They turned their backs on us. Reunion nearly collapsed because of traitors.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: These few fellas didn't shake things up too much. Is there anyone who has never been confused in their life?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: We have our own rules.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: There are other places that could use your help, but you'll go over anyway, right?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Save your strength, avoid combat, go get some suits from Percival and keep yourself safe.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: How did you know—

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: No, forget it.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: That went smoothly. Quite a number recognized you and your fire, Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I already put the shackles back on.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If only they could see my flames as hope.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Now, we have a literal city of Infected.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Can you find a shadow of your former ideals in it?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Only rubble and ruin everywhere I look.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Even we Infected live in our vastly different lives. We suffer from the same disease, but never the same kind of suffering.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: This is why Reunion has to be here.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If the Infected are born from injustice, then we... will stand against all injustice.

steps.name: Londinium Resident
steps.text: You're finally back! Are you hurt, child? The Sarkaz didn't spot you, did they?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I'm fine. Thank you for letting me stay here. I brought some food back with me.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: How are you feeling today?

steps.name: Londinium Resident
steps.text: There's more stones, but it's fine. It doesn't hurt. An old lady like me never had much long to live anyway.

steps.name: Londinium Resident
steps.text: But a group came by while you were gone. They're good people, they gave me a checkup, and I asked them to come back in a bit to examine you too—

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: A checkup? Were they doctors?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: (Rhodes Island should be in the city by now, but I haven't managed to reconnect with them. If that was them...)

steps.name: Londinium Resident
steps.text: Doctors? I'm not sure, but they told me to look for a place with flames if I needed any help.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Flames?

steps.name: Londinium Resident
steps.text: Oh! You're back!

steps.name: Londinium Resident
steps.text: This girl has helped me so much. She's infected too, so take her with you for an examination.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: So it's you.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: It's been a long time, Ch'en.

The artisans who carved the giant statues here many years ago, never could have imagined the guards of the royal mausoleum would collapse into rubble due to the Sarkaz, instead of standing for eternity together with Victoria.
The Feranmut's skeleton emerges from deep underground, landing with a few lucky survivors.
'Ines...where... are we?'

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It's too quiet. We're not on a battlefield... Ines... Ines?!

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Ines! Ines! Hoederer's awake!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Paprika...? Where are we? Where're Ines and W? What's become of the battlefield now? *cough* *cough* Did they recapture the Lifebone already?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Uh... we're currently underground with many stone giants...

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Um... Ines is... W went with the others...

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Wait, hold on, that's too many questions at once—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You recovered quicker than I thought.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I thought he'd be more ruthless with you.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...What of him?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Who knows, Ascalon might have already killed him.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph, don't give me that look.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's good for us if he's really dead.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: But Ines—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Paprika, now's not the time.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Currently, we've stopped the Lifebone in the Mausoleum of Kings. W followed the Doctor and the others to stop the airship, but we don't know how they're doing.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The Mausoleum of Kings? Are you sure—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I recognize the Steam Knights' equipment.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: There's also plenty of Sarkaz remains here, so if my hunch is right...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: This is where the Steam Knights were surrounded and killed back then.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Any other clues?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I did find something.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Take a look.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: This is... clothing?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Found it on a relatively intact Sarkaz skeleton.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I thought it might jog your memories.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: There's a word embroidered in the lining!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...'Julie'?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: 'Julie'? Hoederer, did you know them?
Hoederer shakes his head.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: There aren't many Sarkaz with names, and no way anybody involved in the slaughter here was ordinary.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She left her name here, and it should have stayed undiscovered forever.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But we chanced upon her.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: What she and others did here will ultimately be remembered by us.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: But it sounds like... it wasn't something to be happy about.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We already have more than enough of our own buried in this foreign country after all. How many of them can we remember when everything's over?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: So what next? Your injury—

steps.name: *Radio Noise*
steps.text: Wiš'adel... war... ended—live...

steps.name: *Radio Noise*
steps.text: ...*bzzt*...This is Babel.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Wiš'a...del? Who?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That sounded like—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph. What's she up to this time?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...Have we received any more intelligence from outside the battlefield?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: (Shakes head nervously)

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I fear we might have missed out on something very important—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Grr... He really did try to kill me.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Give yourself some time to heal.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I won't die just yet. Our top priority is to contact the Doctor and W.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: If she wasn't lying in that transmission... then she really needs us now.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It seems like the battle has gone way past how I expected it to go.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Regent, Theresa... what exactly have you two done...?

options: Kal'tsit, the backup plan is working.
We escaped to the underground passage, covered by the chaos of the airship's crash landing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We went through so much in the Assimilated Universe, but Originium's special nature means we were only gone for a brief moment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This will likewise be a sudden change for the Military Commission.

options: It could be a chance for us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Indeed. Communications are being restored, and the ducal alliance will speed up their advance. I don't think the Military Commission will stand a chance against a surrounding offensive from the alliance.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A proactive attack from us might bring greater results, if we rely on the contact points within the city she strived to preserve.

options: It was only because she put herself in danger during this time...
That our backup plan managed to proceed without a hitch.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She did well.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I'd love to hear from Kal'tsit in private about what your group went through, but it really isn't the best time for that.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: To be honest, it was all I could do to bring you out of the chaos.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Many of those in the city saw the airship crash, and everyone has been guessing who's done it.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Doctor, you may find it hard to imagine the joy... when you suddenly see hope within the long dark night...

options: It sounds like it'll benefit our operations in the city.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I wouldn't call it a 'benefit'. At most it means more possibilities for us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Heidi, how did contacting Closure go?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Communications are still being restored, and the city's taken a big hit. We're pressed for time too.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: W... no, she insisted I call her Wiš'adel...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: She said she received a transmission from her subordinates, and took off to verify it. I... couldn't stop her.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No matter. She knows very well what she should be doing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Also, check your belongings. She must have left a way for us to contact her.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: There really is!... When did she leave this beacon on me...?

options: That's very much her style of doing things.
How are Amiya and Logos doing?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The next area hasn't been swept clear yet. Once they confirm it's safe, we'll evacuate to the next safe point at once.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Doctor, Amiya, she...

options: Don't worry about her.
She just needs some time.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Alright. I'll try my best to get in touch with more of our friends inside the city. We'll need their help.

options: I also just compiled all the information we know.
Sync that data with Closure once you manage to connect with her.
I also uploaded arrangements for the other Rhodes Island Operators onto PRTS.
Tell them to update their PRTS as soon as they can so everyone's on the same page.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Seizing the opportunity?

options: Yes.
Currently, every faction in Londinium has their own blind spots.
It's a chance for us to buy time and react to anything in advance.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Understood. I'll handle it—I'm the one most familiar with the rebuilt intracity network after all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You may not have noticed, Doctor. But you've become more proactive ever since we left the Assimilated Universe.

options: ...Is that so?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Is it due to the first Originium?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've become somewhat impatient ever since you met Theresa and learned some truths I'm unable to speak of.

options: I don't think it's a bad thing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I still have my own reservations, but what's important now is to stay clear-headed, and make your judgments.

options: I... why did I betray Theresa back then?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Only Theresa knows the truth to that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will not make any further comments on that incident. But it does not mean my anger towards that event is no more.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: However... Doctor, you have proven yourself to me, to us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You have walked on the same path as us to where we are today, that's enough to prove that Theresa made the right decision.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So, there's no need to be trapped by your past self. Besides, you know absolutely nothing about everything that happened then.

options: That's precisely why... I can't comprehend Theresa's choice at all.
But from her few sentences...
I have a suspicion that fills me with fear.
I have a guess as to what my own mission is.
I'm a savior of this land.
I'm a destroyer of this land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If that is your post-reflection conclusion, I have no objections.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But the you I see before me is still far away from accomplishing that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The path ahead of us is still very, very long... no, perhaps we don't have much time left.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, the future will not wait for us to be ready before it comes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But I will follow you with Rhodes Island down this path.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Can you really say that now with such a calm tone?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're hesitating. You have doubts.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That was never your true self. Do not let unwarranted speculation disturb your present determination.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We determine who we are by our actions than our words. No matter how long we spend hesitating before we reach the end.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The future will answer me, Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am now more willing to follow you down your path.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We will witness it together.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But now, our key focus should be on the thing that can turn the tides of war.

options: The first Originium.
'Amnannam'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa would only hand it over to someone she trusts the most, no matter how the Sarkaz are faring.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa's trust towards Theresis has never changed—they have never truly diverged from one another.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What we currently face is still within the scope of their plan.

options: Theresis...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We have unfinished tasks to get to.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We don't know what Theresis plans to do with a weapon that can easily change this land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There is reason to believe it will not be a gentle method.

options: We need to stop him.
Originium has something to do with me.
I can't absolve myself from the atrocities that happened in Londinium either.
Perhaps this is my mission.
Did you just... smile?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No. Now, have you decided our next course of action, Doctor?

options: Ha, I have a rough idea in mind.
I'll need your help.

a.text: 'Now, the Sarkaz have only one choice left to make, Theresa.'
'Yes... our people have already made their choice.'
'I will fulfil the promise made between us, I will help you.'
'Why do you sigh? I know if I won, you would stand by my side without a shred of hesitation. Isn't that right...'

steps.text: Theresis can no longer hear her voice.
She is gone, but her answer to the future remains.
The first Originium fell from the Shard's peak, traversed the barrier, and landed in the Palace of Westhaleg's subterranean throne room...
The answer already lies in the palm of his hand.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You wrested the key to freedom for the Sarkaz from its arrogant creator.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: As you promised me you would.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But I... lost you, completely.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Theresa, you've fulfilled your promise, so how could I resign myself to walk in your shadow?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I will continue ahead on the path you were halfway through to the end—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: To retrieve what is ours from those who believe they dictate our fate.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I shall judge that arrogant sin.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And this land ought to revere us—
This war, to him, has already ended. And as for the future, the rest will bear witness.
He ignores the ancient seat of Victorian kings caked in dust, and steps into an unknowable darkness.
Theresa has already opened for him, the 'door' to the truth.
He looks forward to what he'll find beyond that door—who will be there to welcome him?
'I have a question. Phantom of a bygone age, who boasts yourself a giant, a god, a supreme creator, one who can dictate the fate of the Sarkaz. Are you truly the only one of your kind...'
'...Dr. {@nickname}?'
